The `named_arg_info` still stores `const Char* name`. So the fix isn't in the `get(name)` function. Let me reconsider.

The crash I reproduced is a heap-buffer-overflow in `strlen` because the argname buffer isn't null-terminated. But the issue description says "Stack-buffer-underflow READ 16". 

Let me reconsider. Maybe the actual oss-fuzz crash is the `values_[-1]` underflow. Let me think about when `is_packed()` is true but `values_[-1]` reads before the actual array.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the `arg_data` layout. In the packed case with named args:

```cpp
template <typename T, typename Char, size_t NUM_ARGS, size_t NUM_NAMED_ARGS>
struct arg_data {
  T args_[1 + (NUM_ARGS != 0 ? NUM_ARGS : 1)];
  named_arg_info<Char> named_args_[NUM_NAMED_ARGS];
  ...
  const T* args() const { return args_ + 1; }
};
```

`args()` returns `args_ + 1`. So `values_ = args_ + 1`. `values_[-1]` = `args_[0]`. This is the value holding `named_args`. Valid.

But what about the NON-named specialization:
```cpp
template <typename T, typename Char, size_t NUM_ARGS>
struct arg_data<T, Char, NUM_ARGS, 0> {
  T args_[NUM_ARGS != 0 ? NUM_ARGS : 1];
  ...
  const T* args() const { return args_; }
};
```

Here `args()` returns `args_`. So `values_ = args_`. `values_[-1]` = `args_[-1]`, which is BEFORE the array! This is the stack-buffer-underflow!

But wait, this specialization is used when `num_named_args == 0`. In that case, `has_named_args()` is false, so `get(name)` returns early. So `values_[-1]` is never accessed.

Hmm, unless... Let me reconsider. Is there a case where `has_named_args()` is true but the non-named arg_data specialization is used? 

`has_named_args()` checks `desc_ & has_named_args_bit`. `desc` is set as:
```cpp
static constexpr unsigned long long desc =
    (is_packed ? internal::encode_types<Context, Args...>()
               : internal::is_unpacked_bit | num_args) |
    (num_named_args != 0
         ? static_cast<unsigned long long>(internal::has_named_args_bit)
         : 0);
```

So `has_named_args_bit` is set iff `num_named_args != 0`. And the named arg_data specialization is used iff `num_named_args != 0`. So they're consistent.

Hmm. So the `values_[-1]` underflow shouldn't happen in the normal flow. Let me reconsider.

The `named_args.data[i].name` is a `const Char*`. When compared with `name` (a `basic_string_view`), it constructs a `basic_string_view` from the `const Char*`:

```cpp

```cpp
template <typename T, typename Char>

  const T& value;
  named_arg(basic_string_view<Char> name, const T& val)
      : named_arg_base<Char>(name), value(val) {}
};
```

`named_arg_base<Char>`:
```cpp
template <typename Char> struct named_arg_base {
  basic_string_view<Char> name;   // 16 bytes
  mutable char data[sizeof(basic_format_arg<buffer_context<Char>>)];  // 24 bytes
  ...
};
```

```cpp
template <typename Context> basic_format_arg<Context> deserialize() const {
    basic_format_arg<Context> arg;
    std::memcpy(&arg, data, sizeof(basic_format_arg<Context>));
    return arg;
}
```

`data` is 24 bytes (sizeof basic_format_arg<buffer_context<char>>). `deserialize<format_context>` copies `sizeof(basic_format_arg<format_context>)` bytes. If these are equal (24 bytes), no issue.
